business.description: Everest Industries Limited is a building solutions company with a 92-year legacy, offering roofing solutions, boards & panels, and pre-engineered steel buildings. It operates 9 manufacturing plants, a distribution network of 14,000+ dealer outlets, and serves 1,00,000+ villages across India and 35+ international markets.

outlook.statement: The Company's variable margin improved by 3.6 points in the second half as compared to the first. The Company's gross margin improved by 1.7 points in the second half as compared to the first. The Company's Sales & General Administrative expenses were reduced by Rs. 9.9 crores in the second half as compared to the first half. Most importantly, while the Company's free operating cash flow after capex was Rs. (29) crores in the first half, it improved to Rs. 128 crores in the second half.
I am now very confident that the Company will only grow from strength to strength across all its three businesses, and that FY 2026-27 will be a year that you will be proud of.

We enter FY 2026-27 with far greater strategic clarity, strong leadership team, deep organizational alignment, and a renewed commitment to operational excellence, customer centricity, and profitable growth.
India's structural growth drivers—including rural development, urbanisation, industrial expansion, and infrastructure investment—continue to create significant opportunities for our businesses.

India's economic outlook for FY27 remains positive with Economic Survey projecting real GDP growth of 6.8-7.2%. Domestic demand, favourable agricultural prospects, GST rationalisation effects, and strong corporate/banking balance sheets to bolster activity. Infrastructure capex budgeted at record Rs. 12.2 lakh crore for FY27 will provide strong demand visibility for construction and building materials.

Differentiated products and system solutions will enable Everest to maintain competitive advantage across customer segments. Programmes such as PMAY, rural development and allied infrastructure investments to support long-term demand for cost-effective roofing solutions.

PEB business will strengthen presence in high-growth sectors (warehousing, food processing, e-commerce logistics, solar module manufacturing), advance engineering excellence through structural innovation and smart steel technologies, reduce project cycle times via digital design tools and partner-led execution, and deliver integrated turnkey solutions combining insulation, solar-ready roofing and mezzanine systems.

Boards & Panels industry estimated at ~1 million MT (Rs 1,800 crores) expected to grow at 10-12% CAGR over next 5-7 years. Focus on solidifying industry leadership through differentiated products, system solutions, architect engagement platforms, contractor skilling and Contractor Loyalty Program.

Long-term outlook for the roofing industry remains stable, supported by sustained demand for affordable, durable, and easy-to-install roofing solutions, particularly across rural and semi-urban markets.

Expected growth in hospitality, healthcare, commercial real estate, infrastructure, and increasing development of data centres are likely to drive strong growth for fibre cement boards over the next decade.
PEB market is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 12% in the next 5 years.
Record infrastructure capex of Rs. 11.2 lakh crore in FY26, rising to Rs. 12.2 lakh crore in FY27, is creating strong structural demand for building materials.
Company is well positioned to be profitable in 2026-27 after recognising one-time charges and implementing cost optimisation.
Geopolitical uncertainties could impact exports in the short term.

The Company has put in place plans and strategic initiatives for achieving sustainable growth and turning performance to profitability. The Company is focusing on execution, quality, service, pricing, value added sales, cost, productivity and volume. Some of the steps taken by the Company are strengthening product portfolio, manufacturing capability, marketing initiatives and optimising cost of manufacturing and in general cost reduction.
Everest Steel Building Private Limited's PEB manufacturing plant setup deferred to FY 2026-27
Everest keeps on exploring a two-pronged approach aimed at improving energy efficiency and evaluating the potential for renewable energy integration.
The Company plans to generate at least 50% of its Boards and Panels division revenue from EPD-certified products by 2027.
The Company aims to focus on low-carbon products.

Everest is considering a broader evaluation of renewable energy options across its facilities to potentially lower Scope 2 emissions and improve long-term resource efficiency. The company aims to reduce and replenish groundwater it consumes over the next 2-3 years. Plans to undertake Life Cycle Assessments for key products within the Boards and Panels division. Prioritizing domestic sourcing and diversifying supplier base for critical imports like pulp and asbestos fiber. Focusing on advancing Health and Safety standards and fostering a truly inclusive and diverse workplace. Building a comprehensive ESG assessment framework for supply chain.

Advancing a comprehensive strategy to reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions through energy efficiency, renewable energy adoption with a focus on electricity and fuels consumed, and responsible product stewardship.

Evaluating group captive open access models to potentially scale renewable electricity use. A broader feasibility study is underway to assess the viability of extending these initiatives across locations.

Multiple energy efficiency projects are underway, with particular emphasis on reducing Units/MT across Business Units—initially targeting Roofing and ESBS. Additional initiatives include adoption of Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), rigorous preventive maintenance, and other energy-saving interventions.

Conducting Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of Boards and Panels business to quantify environmental impacts, identify emission hotspots, implement low-carbon materials and technologies, and optimize processes to support GHG emissions reduction targets.
Integrated approach across operations, energy sources, and product innovation reflects firm commitment to decarbonization and long-term climate resilience.

Health & Safety Risk: Manufacturing operations involve interactions with machinery and material-handling equipment, posing inherent safety risks to employees.
Water Risk: Heavy reliance on groundwater for manufacturing; water scarcity and regulatory scrutiny increase operational risks. Two plants (Podanur, Bhagwanpur) in semi-critical groundwater zones.

Supply Chain Risk: Value chain is resource- and energy-intensive, relying on raw materials like cement and steel with significant environmental impacts. Supplier non-compliance could expose company to reputational and regulatory risks.
Business Ethics Risk: Non-compliance with regulations or failure to prevent unethical practices could lead to financial losses, legal penalties, reputational damage.
Labour Relations Risk: Disruption in manufacturing due to labour unrest or compliance issues.
Risk Management: Without proactive identification and mitigation of risks, companies are ill-prepared for unexpected events like regulatory changes, supply chain breakdowns, environmental incidents.

Revenue recognition involves usage of input method which is determined based on proportion of contract costs incurred to date compared to estimated total contract costs, which involves significant judgments, identification of contractual obligations and the Company's rights to receive payments for performance completed till date, risk on collectability due to liquidated damages, other penalties imposed by the customers, changes in scope and consequential revised contract price and recognition of the liability for loss making contracts / onerous obligations.

The Company has ongoing disputes with the Income tax departments on income tax computation for certain assessment years. These disputes are pending with different Appellate authorities and at the Courts. The management has assessed the future outcome of these ongoing proceedings and exposures which directly affects the valuation of tax provision and estimation with regard to the existing tax disputes and uncertain tax positions.

The Company has invested in, and extended loan to, its subsidiary. As at March 31, 2026, the gross carrying amount of such investment and loan is Rs. 1,703.55 lakhs and Rs. 10,777.66 lakhs, respectively. The subsidiary continues to incur losses and its net worth stands negative as at March 31, 2026. During the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized impairment allowances of Rs. 1,500.88 lakhs on its investment in the subsidiary and Rs. 1,369.12 lakhs on the loan extended to the subsidiary, respectively.
